q: Bronsted-Lowry acid is a proton donor. (2024)
e: According to the Bronsted-Lowry theory, an acid is defined as a proton (H+) donor.

q: Buffers are very important to chemical and biological systems. (2024)
e: Buffer solutions maintain a stable pH environment, which is vital for biochemical reactions and cellular processes.

q: NH3 molecule behaves as a Lewis acid which donates an electron pair. (2024)
e: NH3 acts as a Lewis base because it donates an electron pair, whereas a Lewis acid accepts an electron pair.

q: The dissociation constant of a weaker acid is greater than that of a stronger acid. (2024)
e: A stronger acid dissociates to a greater extent and therefore has a larger dissociation constant (Ka) than a weaker acid.

q: The value of Kw is approximately 5.6 × 10^-3 mol^2 dm^-6 at 100°C. (2024)
e: The value of Kw at 100°C is approximately 5.6 × 10^-13 mol^2 dm^-6.

q: Conjugate acid is a species that forms when a base gains a proton. (2025)
e: When a base accepts a proton, it is converted into its conjugate acid.

q: Conjugate base is a species that forms when a base gains a proton. (2025)
e: A conjugate base is formed when an acid loses or donates a proton.

q: The conjugate base of a Brönsted-Lowry acid is the species that remains when one proton has been added to the acid. (2025)
e: The conjugate base is the species remaining after a proton has been removed from the acid.

q: If the Kb value for anion and Ka value for cation in an aqueous solution are equal, the pH of an aqueous solution will be 7. (2025)
e: When Ka of the cation equals Kb of the anion, the extent of acidic and basic hydrolysis balances out to leave a neutral pH of 7.

q: The pH of 0.001 mol dm^-3 of hydrochloric acid is 11. (2025)
e: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid; a 0.001 mol dm^-3 solution has a pH of 3.

q: CH3COO^- ion is a strong conjugate base. (2025)
e: Because CH3COOH is a weak acid, its conjugate base CH3COO^- is relatively strong.

q: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that partially ionise only to a limited extent in water. (2025)
e: Weak acids undergo partial ionisation in aqueous solution, classifying them as weak electrolytes.

q: Pure water undergoes ionisation to a very high extent. (2025)
e: Pure water undergoes autoionisation only to a very slight extent.

q: Ammonia molecule accepts a proton from water forming NH4^+ ion and this ion is strong conjugate acid. (2025)
e: Since NH3 is a weak base, its conjugate acid (NH4^+) acts as a relatively strong conjugate acid.

q: The dissociation constant of a base increases as the strength of the base decreases. (2025)
e: The dissociation constant (Kb) increases as the strength of the base increases.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of three protons are called diprotic acids. (2026)
e: Given as True in the answer key.

q: Ammonium ethanoate solution is acidic. (2026)
e: Ammonium ethanoate is formed from a weak acid and a weak base with equal dissociation strengths, making the solution neutral.

q: Arrhenius proposed that acids are any substances that dissociate to produce hydrogen ions when they dissolve in water. (2026)
e: The classical Arrhenius theory defines an acid as a compound that increases H+ concentration in aqueous solution.

q: A buffer solution of pH 7-11 can be prepared with a weak acid and its salt. (2026)
e: A buffer solution in the alkaline range (pH 7–11) is made using a weak base and its salt.

q: Salt hydrolysis usually affects the concentration of a solution. (2026)
e: Salt hydrolysis affects the pH (ion concentrations of H+ and OH-) of the solution rather than the overall molar concentration of the salt.

q: The pH scale ranges from 1 to 14. (2026)
e: The standard pH scale ranges from 0 to 14.
